text:
maria: FYI — after the gpu-operator v1.5.0 rollout across us-west1/us-east1 we started seeing a handful of nodes report GPU allocatable=0 and pods Pending (Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu).
chris: confirmed in #monitoring — spike around 03:12UTC, ~12 nodes affected, mixed A100/V100 fleet.
raj: do we have any kubelet logs from the affected nodes? sounds like device-plugin didn't register after driver install.
olivia: grabbing logs now, but short dump: `kubelet[pid]: device plugin: Advertise() called before driver probe` in several nodes. also seeing `nvidia-modprobe: failed to load module` on a couple.
kevin: that sounds like kernel-module vs driver mismatch — some nodes still on kernel 5.15, driver image expects 5.19-ish symbols. Did the node reboot sequence change during upgrade?
infra-bot: Deploy started by deploy-bot: gpu-operator v1.5.0 -> rollout in progress -> 120/200 nodes targeted.
chris: we rolled kube 1.27 last night; ordering might have made kubelet restart before the operator finished installing drivers. device-plugin is up earlier than host driver. race condition.
raj: interesting — also seeing NCCL errors in trainer pods on nodes that were *not* marked Allocatable=0: `nccl: CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version` — suggests driver older than container CUDA runtime.
maria: so two parallel issues: (1) device-plugin/driver install order causing advertise-before-probe -> allocatable 0, (2) driver/CUDA runtime mismatch -> NCCL failures and OOMs.
olivia: attaching a representative node log snippet: ```
[Apr 10 03:11:58] nvidia-installer: Driver 525.85 installed
[Apr 10 03:12:03] kubelet: device-plugin started, Advertise() -> registered GPUs: 0
[Apr 10 03:12:05] modprobe: nvidia: FATAL: Module nvidia not found in directory /lib/modules/5.15.0-101-generic
```
chris: can we mark affected nodes with `gpu-ready=false` and prevent new scheduling? taint + nodeSelector until we fix drivers.
kevin: yes, `kubectl taint node <node> gpu-ready=false:NoSchedule` will block new pods. Also scale down everything using GPUs on those nodes.
raj: proposal: rollback gpu-operator to v1.4.3 (previous stable) in us-west1 only, and run a manual canary in us-east1 with a handful nodes patched with correct kernel headers.
maria: agree on canary. If rollback is quick we can revert operator changes that altered the driver install cr. chris can you run the rollback?
chris: on it. `kubectl -n gpu-operator rollout undo deploy/gpu-operator --to-revision=3` planning to do a pairwise rollback, will confirm.
olivia: I will prepare node script to check kernel headers and driver probe before untainting: simple check: `ls /lib/modules/$(uname -r)/kernel/drivers/video/nvidia || exit 1` — only remove taint if probe OK.
kevin: also we should add a preflight KUDO check in the operator: ensure `modprobe nvidia` succeeds and `nvidia-smi` returns GPUs>0 before advertising. file a GH issue.
raj: note on cost/ops: a bunch of Pending pods are scaling up replicas in other regions and consuming spot pools — cost spike in us-east due to autoscaler. we should pause autoscaler rules for GPU-backed ASGs while we heal.
maria: put autoscaler on hold for GPU ASGs globally for the next 2 hours. I'll message infra-runbook.
sre-oncall: I've muted alerts noisy from training queues and created a temporary incident: INC-2026. Owning until rollout completes.
chris: rolled back us-west1 gpu-operator -> rollout paused at 02:58UTC, verifying node state. current plan: rollback, taint affected nodes, patch driver daemonset ordering, then gradual untaint.
olivia: for the long-term fix: operator should add a readiness probe for the driver daemonset containers and only allow device-plugin deployment after that readiness is green. I'll draft a patch.
raj: also, add NCCL runtime/driver compatibility matrix to the operator's model catalog so we can block images with mismatched CUDA versions during admission. prevents `CUDA driver version is insufficient` class errors.
kevin: assign follow-ups: chris -> rollback + taint/untaint playbook, raj -> NCCL/compat matrix PR, olivia -> node preflight script + readiness probe PR, maria -> autoscaler pause + incident comms.
maria: timeline: 0-15m rollback, 15-45m canary checks, 45-120m staged reapply with readiness gating.
chris: rollback done for control plane in us-west1, initiating node-level driver re-provision on canary set.
raj: running validation script across canary nodes: `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version,name --format=csv` -> shows 525.85 on canary, kernel headers present. Allocatable restored on canary.
maria: good. if canary OK, we'll roll forward with patched operator that enforces probe-before-advertise.
olivia: opened PR #432 for readiness gating + added unit test that simulates missing kernel headers.
kevin: GH issue for better daemonset ordering labeled `P0` and assigned to eng-infra.
infra-bot: INC-2026 updated: rollback completed for region us-west1; monitoring set to 30s.
maria: thanks everyone — keep updates here. postmortem draft after incident closed, include root cause (race during operator rollout + kernel mismatch) and remediation (readiness gating, compat matrix, autoscaler safe mode). :white_check_mark:
